officialDocumentation.finding: The app-server accepts additional input on the active turn and returns its turn identifier. It does not start a separate turn for that request.

officialDocumentation.section: Queue input and handle the continuation
officialDocumentation.finding: Responses steering acceptance acknowledges queued input. Application of the update can wait for current output and hosted work to finish.
officialDocumentation.qualification: This documents the current Responses API. It does not establish that pinned Codex 0.160.1 used that exact transport or account route during these recordings.

sourceFindings.claim: The application permits one outstanding input frame before submitting another changed final question.
Its once-only second attempt disables the short final-refinement restart deadline.
The configured short final-refinement wait is 400ms, not a fixed ten-second sleep.
The reply acknowledgement is distinct from the later matching userMessage consumption event.
The normal HTTP client has a ten-second connect timeout. Codex automatic answering takes the native app-server branch; that HTTP timeout is not evidence of a ten-second sleep on its steering path.
The selected Codex answer branch uses native app-server question updates.
The nominal 8000-character value is not an enforced cap on the complete composite context.
Exact code/prior-answer history is appended after selected transcript sections.
The code archive evicts whole earlier entries when its archive budget is exceeded and preserves one accepted entry, even if its paired question takes it over the budget.
The history-character heuristic suppresses extra partial refinements after the budget is spent; changed confirmed inputs still follow the final-update path.
The 80000-character condition restricts later native-history reuse; it is not a model token limit or a hard cap on all confirmed inputs within the current attempt.

The final-only control suppresses generation from candidate transcript changes. It still uses the normal confirmed-question route, so an internal pause can produce a confirmed fragment before the utterance continues.

conclusion: The final-update serialization and disabled second-attempt short deadline are application mechanisms that permit long waits. The fresh recorded tail has no observed per-thread full queue and negligible reader-to-consumer processing delay. The ten-second pre-receipt interval cannot be assigned to a fixed HTTP connect wait or to provider-internal reasoning from these observations. Ongoing old-frame generation and repeated context transmission remain hypotheses to distinguish with event trajectories and matched fresh-meeting controls.

controls.selection: Slowest retained visible word and the nearest observed median from each of three freshly completed hours, subject to a bound recorded context and waveform. No correctness filter.
controls.limitations: Selected dependent cases do not estimate population p95. Final-only waits for normal confirmations, not a known physical end of a multipart question. The original full-hour cohort retains every turn.
